scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026/Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-sparsest-cut-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 117 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 75f6af00a38589bf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed real constant C > 1, there is a polynomial-time reduction from 3CNF satisfiability to finite undirected graphs with nonnegative rational capacities and exactly unit demands, together with a positive rational threshold a, such that the formula is satisfiable =⇒ Φ(G) ≤ a, the formula is unsatisfiable =⇒ Φ(G) > Ca. The graph size and the bit lengths of all output numbers are polynomial in the formula size, with constants and exponents allowed to depend on C. In particular, approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed factor C > 1 is NP-hard.
